html:
Company: Bottled wine producer · Home country: China · Size: Small (<50 staff) · HS 220421 (Agri-food & beverages) · Generated 2026-11-21

1. Executive Summary

Verdict: ENTER WITH CAUTION. Real opportunity, but specific risks need a mitigation plan before scaling.

Market attractiveness: 5.6/10
Recommended entry mode: Indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors

  • Import market of €1.10 bn in 2024, growing -11.04% a year since 2019.
  • Supply is moderately concentrated (HHI 1,239); top supplier Chile holds 21.23%.
  • CAGE distance from China: high.
  • China supplies 0.2% of extra-EU imports.
  • Priority EU markets: Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark.

4. PESTEL Analysis

  • Political: Stable democracies with a single trade policy run by the European Commission. EU-China relations follow a 'de-risking' agenda: more trade-defence cases, the Foreign Subsidies Regulation and screening of Chinese investment.
  • Economic: Single market of ~450 million consumers and one of the world's largest import markets; high purchasing power, though growth is modest and varies strongly between member states. Latest: GDP growth 1.5% (2025), inflation 2.5% (World Bank).
  • Social: Diverse languages and consumer cultures across 27 countries; strong demand for sustainability, quality and data privacy; ageing population.
  • Technological: Advanced digital infrastructure and e-commerce; strict standards (CE, EN norms) make quality and certification a competitive factor.
  • Environmental: European Green Deal: CBAM, Ecodesign/ESPR, Battery Regulation, deforestation and packaging rules raise compliance costs but reward low-carbon products.
  • Legal: Harmonised product law across the EU (one CE mark for 27 markets), GDPR for customer data, strong IP protection and contract enforcement. Sanitary and phytosanitary rules can block market access entirely.

5. CAGE Distance

Dimension Distance Evidence
Cultural Medium The EU spans 24 official languages; expect local-language marketing, labels and service in each priority country.
Administrative High No free-trade agreement: MFN tariffs, separate standards and customs procedures.
Geographic High ~7,962 km between capitals. Long lead times (Asia-Europe sea freight ~30-45 days; China-Europe rail ~15-20 days).
Economic High GDP per capita $13,862 (home) vs $47,089 (target), ratio 3.4x.

Overall distance: High.

6. Tariffs, Trade Defence & Regulation

⚠️ Trade defence: EU wine faces strong competition from Australia in China since China lifted its duties on Australian wine in 2024.

  • Food hygiene and official controls (Reg. 852/2004, 2017/625); border checks for animal and plant products
  • Food Information to Consumers Reg. 1169/2011 (labelling in the local language)
  • EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) for cocoa, coffee, soy, palm oil, cattle, wood and rubber
  • General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 (GPSR), applies to consumer products since Dec 2024
  • Union Customs Code: an EU-established importer/representative and EORI number are required
  • Forced Labour Regulation (EU) 2024/3015: ban on products made with forced labour, applies from Dec 2027

Verify current duties and requirements: - Access2Markets (EU tariffs, rules of origin, requirements) - EU TARIC tariff database - EU trade defence cases

7. Risk Matrix

Risk Likelihood Impact Mitigation
Shrinking import demand High Medium Target growing niches or member states; validate demand before fixed investment.
Trade-defence or retaliation measures in the EU-China corridor High High Monitor trade-defence notices; diversify sourcing and production locations; build tariff scenarios into pricing.
Long regulatory approval / registration timeline High High Start registration early with a local regulatory agent; budget 6-24 months.
Logistics disruption (Red Sea, port congestion, freight-rate swings) Medium Medium Use mixed sea/rail routing, safety stock in a regional hub, Incoterms that share freight risk.
Brand and message mis-fit with local consumers Medium Medium Local consumer testing, native-language content, local marketplace and social channels.
Currency volatility (EUR/CNY/USD) Medium Medium Price in home currency where possible; hedge large contracts with forwards.

8. Recommended Entry Mode

Indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors

  • Moderate attractiveness or high distance favour a low-commitment, reversible entry.
  • Keeps capital at risk low while you learn the market.
  • Within the EU one CE-compliant product and one importer of record give access to all 27 markets: start with 2-3 priority countries.
  • Inputs: attractiveness 5.6/10, CAGE distance high, institutional quality 6.8/10, company size small (<50 staff).

10. 90-Day Action Plan

  1. Days 1-30, validate: confirm the HS code and duty rate on official tariff tools, size the niche with customer interviews, shortlist 10 potential partners or channels in Luxembourg, Netherlands, Denmark.
  2. Days 1-30, compliance: map required certifications and labelling (see section 6), get quotes from a test lab or regulatory agent, register trademarks in the target market.
  3. Days 1-30, registration: file the product registration / notification early: it is the critical path.
  4. Days 31-60, commercial model: build a landed-cost and pricing model (duties, freight, VAT, channel margins, FX), and draft the partner or channel agreement.
  5. Days 31-60, go-to-market: localise product pages, packaging and sales material; pick 1-2 launch channels consistent with the entry mode: indirect / direct exporting via importers and distributors.
  6. Days 61-90, pilot: ship a pilot order or open the online store, track sell-through, margin and customer feedback against go/no-go KPIs.
